words.en: Service provided by a company or store after a product has been sold, including support, maintenance, and repairs.

words.ex: The air crash happened last night.
words.ex_cn: 空难发生在昨晚。
words.en: An air crash is an accident in which an aircraft is destroyed or damaged as a result of a collision, especially while in flight.

words.ex: He flipped through the album with old photos.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看着装满旧照片的相册。
words.en: An album is a collection of several pieces of music, songs, or photographs that are intended to form a single item.

words.tr: adj. 全能的；多方面的；多才多艺的
words.ex: He is an all-round athlete who plays soccer, basketball, and tennis.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名全能运动员，踢足球、打篮球和打网球。
words.en: Having a wide range of abilities or uses; versatile.

words.ex: He is an alumnus of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 他是哈佛大学的男毕业生。
words.en: An alumnus is a former student of a particular school, college, or university.

words.tr: n. 反腐败，反贪腐；廉政风暴
words.ex: The government launched an anti-corruption campaign.
words.ex_cn: 政府发起了一项反腐败运动。
words.en: Opposed to or intended to prevent corruption.

words.ex: He is argumentative in class and always disagrees with the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他在课堂上爱争辩，总是不同意老师的意见。
words.en: Someone who is argumentative is always ready to disagree or start arguing with other people.

words.tr: phrase. 集会大厅；礼堂（用于学校、机构等举行集会、仪式或活动的场所）
words.ex: The assembly hall was filled with students for the annual speech.
words.ex_cn: 礼堂里挤满了来听年度演讲的学生。
words.en: A large room or building used for gatherings or meetings, especially in a school or community setting.

words.ex: Workers stand on the assembly line to put parts together.
words.ex_cn: 工人们站在装配线上组装零件。
words.en: An assembly line is a manufacturing process in which parts are added to a product in a sequential manner to create a finished product.

words.ex: The assemblyman proposed a new bill on environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 这位议员提出了一项新的环境保护法案。
words.en: An assemblyman is a man who is a member of a legislative assembly, especially in the United States.

words.ex: He works as an assistant secretary in the office.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室担任助理秘书。
words.en: An assistant secretary is a person who assists a secretary in their duties, often in a government or large organization, handling administrative tasks and supporting the management.

words.tr: phrase. 国务副部长（美国国务院中仅次于国务卿和副国务卿的高级官员）
words.ex: The assistant secretary of state for East Asian and Pacific Affairs is responsible for the U.S. foreign policy in the region.
words.ex_cn: 负责东亚和太平洋事务的助理国务卿负责美国在该地区的外交政策。
words.en: An assistant secretary of state is a high-ranking official in the United States Department of State, responsible for assisting the Secretary of State in managing the department's operations and policies.

words.ex: The atomic nucleus is the central part of an atom, consisting of protons and neutrons.
words.ex_cn: 原子核是原子的中心部分，由质子和中子组成。
words.en: The central part of an atom, consisting of protons and neutrons, and containing nearly all its mass.

words.tr: phrase. 观众收视率；听众或观众对节目受欢迎程度的评价
words.ex: The show's audience rating has been steadily increasing.
words.ex_cn: 该节目的收视率一直在稳步上升。
words.en: The percentage of the total number of households or individuals tuned to a specific television or radio program at a given time.

words.tr: n. 高保真音响爱好者
words.ex: He spent a fortune on his audiophile equipment.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的高保真音响设备花了一大笔钱。
words.en: An audiophile is a person who is enthusiastic about high-fidelity sound reproduction.

words.tr: phrase. 权威的；可信的；有权威性的信息
words.ex: The website provides authoritative information about health.
words.ex_cn: 这个网站提供关于健康的权威信息。
words.en: Information that is considered reliable and accurate, often coming from a recognized expert or source.

words.tr: phrase. 权威的；可信的；可信赖的 来源
words.ex: The website is an authoritative source for health information.
words.ex_cn: 这个网站是健康信息的权威来源。
words.en: An authoritative source is a source that is recognized as reliable and accurate, often used in research and academic work.

words.tr: phrase. 单身母亲（指未婚女子成为母亲）
words.ex: She is a bachelor mother raising her child alone.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位独自抚养孩子的单身母亲。
words.en: A woman who has a child or children but is not married.

words.tr: phrase. 背景简报；情况介绍（通常指非公开的、为提供信息而进行的说明）
words.ex: The spokesperson held a background briefing to provide context for the upcoming policy changes.
words.ex_cn: 发言人举行了一次背景情况介绍会，为即将到来的政策变化提供背景信息。
words.en: A background briefing is a meeting or document that provides detailed information and context on a particular subject, often to prepare someone for an event or discussion.

words.ex: Bacteria can make you sick.
words.ex_cn: 细菌会让你生病。
words.en: Bacteria are very small organisms. Some bacteria can cause diseases.

words.tr: n. 弹幕射击；掩护炮火；拦河坝
words.ex: The soldiers faced a barrage of bullets.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们面对着一阵弹雨。
words.en: A barrage is a heavy and continuous bombardment of gunfire or a dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

words.ex: He used a beeper to stay in touch with his team.
words.ex_cn: 他使用传呼机与团队保持联系。
words.en: A beeper is a small device you carry that makes a noise to tell you when someone is trying to contact you.

words.ex: This test is a benchmark for all students.
words.ex_cn: 这个测试是所有学生的标准。
words.en: A benchmark is something whose quality or quantity is known and which can therefore be used as a standard with which other things can be compared.

words.tr: phrase. 慈善音乐会；为筹集善款或支持某项事业而举办的演出
words.ex: A benefit concert was held to raise funds for the flood victims.
words.ex_cn: 为洪水灾民筹集资金而举办了一场慈善音乐会。
words.en: A benefit concert is a musical performance held to raise funds for a charitable cause.

words.tr: phrase. 抬高价格；通过出价竞争使价格上升
words.ex: Bidders bid up the price of the antique vase.
words.ex_cn: 竞标者抬高了那件古董花瓶的价格。
words.en: To increase the price of something by offering higher bids, often in an auction or competitive market.

words.tr: phrase. 重要人物；举足轻重的人；大炮
words.ex: He is considered a big gun in the financial industry.
words.ex_cn: 他被认为是金融界的重要人物。
words.en: A big gun is a person who is very important or influential, especially in a particular field.

words.tr: phrase. 大谎言；指一个巨大而明显的谎言，常被用来操纵公众舆论
words.ex: The politician's big lie about his past was eventually exposed.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客关于他过去的弥天大谎最终被揭穿了。
words.en: A big lie is a lie which attempts to trick the victim into believing something major which will likely be contradicted by some information the victim already possesses, or by their common sense.

words.tr: n. 小饭店；小餐馆；小酒馆
words.ex: We had coffee at a small bistro near the park.
words.ex_cn: 我们在公园附近的一家小酒馆喝了咖啡。
words.en: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant or a small bar or nightclub.

words.tr: phrase. 黑匣子（指飞机上的飞行记录仪）；不透明的系统（其内部运作无法被观察或理解）
words.ex: The black box in an airplane records flight data and cockpit conversations.
words.ex_cn: 飞机上的黑匣子记录飞行数据和驾驶舱对话。
words.en: A device in an aircraft that records information about its performance and condition, used for investigating accidents.

words.tr: phrase. 黑市价格；指在非法或非官方市场上商品或服务的交易价格
words.ex: The black market price for the medicine is significantly higher than the official rate.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物的黑市价格明显高于官方价格。
words.en: The price of goods or services sold illegally, often higher than the official or legal price due to scarcity or regulation.

words.tr: n. 一阵强劲的气流；爆炸；
words.ex: A blast of cold wind hit the window.
words.ex_cn: 一阵冷风击中了窗户。
words.en: A blast is a sudden loud noise or a strong gust of wind. It can also refer to an explosion or the act of blowing something up. As a verb, it means to explode or to criticize severely.

words.tr: phrase. 死胡同；没有出路的困境；无法取得进展的途径
words.ex: The project turned out to be a blind alley, and we had to abandon it.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目结果成了死胡同，我们不得不放弃它。
words.en: A blind alley is a street or passage that is closed at one end, or a situation or activity that leads nowhere or has no future.

words.tr:
n. 阻塞；封锁
v. 封锁
words.ex: The blockade stopped all ships from entering the port.
words.ex_cn: 封锁阻止了所有船只进入港口。
words.en: A blockade is an action to prevent goods or people from entering or leaving a place.

words.tr: phrase. 不流血的政变；指通过和平或非暴力手段实现的政权更迭
words.ex: The transition of power was achieved through a bloodless coup.
words.ex_cn: 权力的过渡是通过一场不流血政变实现的。
words.en: A bloodless coup is a change of government that occurs without any violence or bloodshed.

words.tr: phrase. 追回；收回（已支付的款项、收益等）
words.ex: The government is planning to claw back the funds that were misappropriated.
words.ex_cn: 政府正计划追回被挪用的资金。
words.en: To regain or recover something, especially money or rights, through effort or legal means.

words.ex: The new medicine went through a clinical trial last year.
words.ex_cn: 这种新药去年进行了临床试验。
words.en: A clinical trial is a research study that tests how well new medical approaches work in people. These studies test new methods of screening, prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of a disease.

words.tr: adj. 昏迷不醒的；不省人事的；困乏的
words.ex: The man became comatose after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，这个人陷入了昏迷。
words.en: If someone is comatose, they are in a coma and are not conscious.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.ex: The denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula remains a complex issue.
words.ex_cn: 朝鲜半岛的无核化仍然是一个复杂的问题。
words.en: The process of reducing or eliminating nuclear weapons or nuclear capabilities from a country or region.

words.ex: He faced public denunciation for his lies.
words.ex_cn: 他因撒谎而遭到公众的谴责。
words.en: Denunciation is the act of criticizing something or someone strongly and publicly.

words.tr: adj. 实际的；脚踏实地的
words.ex: He is a down-to-earth man who helps everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个脚踏实地的人，乐于帮助每个人。
words.en: If you say that someone is down-to-earth, you approve of the fact that they concern themselves with practical things and actions, rather than with abstract theories.

words.tr: phrase. 极度兴奋的状态；狂热的高潮
words.ex: The crowd reached fever pitch as the final goal was scored.
words.ex_cn: 随着最后一球的得分，人群达到了极度兴奋的状态。
words.en: A state of extreme excitement or agitation.

words.ex: The rope is 100 footage long.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子长100英尺。
words.en: Footage refers to a sequence of film or video that has been shot, especially when it is used in a news broadcast or a documentary.

words.ex: The walls had colorful graffiti on them.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有着五颜六色的涂画。
words.en: Graffiti is words or pictures that are written or drawn in public places, for example on walls or posters.

words.ex: He picked up the handset to call his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起手机给妈妈打电话。
words.en: A handset is a device that is held in the hand, especially one that is used as part of a telephone or radio.

words.ex: The police raided the gang's hideout.
words.ex_cn: 警方突袭了该团伙的藏匿处。
words.en: A hideout is a place where someone can go to hide away from other people.

words.tr: phrase. v. 推迟；阻挡；抑制；保持距离
words.ex: Please hold off until tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 请等到明天再做。
words.en: To delay doing something, or to prevent something from happening or someone from doing something.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 躲藏起来；隐蔽
words.ex: During the storm, we decided to hole up in the cabin.
words.ex_cn: 在暴风雨期间，我们决定躲在小屋里。
words.en: To hide or take refuge, especially to avoid being found or to escape from something.

words.ex: The books are placed in a row on the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 书整齐地摆成一排放在书架上。
words.en: If something happens several times in a row, it happens that number of times without a break.

words.ex: He spilled ink on his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他把墨水洒在了衬衫上。
words.en: Ink is the colored liquid used for writing, printing, or drawing.

words.tr: phrase. 非物质文化遗产；指被社区、群体或个人视为其文化遗产组成部分的各种实践、表现、表达、知识和技能，以及与之相关的工具、物品、工艺品和文化场所
words.ex: China protects its intangible cultural heritage like paper cutting and folk music.
words.ex_cn: 中国保护其非物质文化遗产，如剪纸和民间音乐。
words.en: Intangible cultural heritage refers to the practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, skills – as well as the instruments, objects, artifacts and cultural spaces associated therewith – that communities, groups and, in some cases, individuals recognize as part of their cultural heritage.

words.tr: phrase. 临时政府；过渡政府
words.ex: The interim government was established to oversee the transition of power.
words.ex_cn: 临时政府成立是为了监督权力的过渡。
words.en: A temporary government that is established to manage a country until a permanent government is elected.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: The kidnapper took the boy and demanded money.
words.ex_cn: 绑匪绑架了那个男孩并索要赎金。
words.en: A kidnapper is a person who abducts someone and holds them captive, typically to demand a ransom.

words.tr: n. 售货亭；报刊亭；公用电话亭
words.ex: He bought a ticket from the kiosk.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动售票机买了一张票。
words.en: A kiosk is a small open-fronted hut or cubicle from which newspapers, refreshments, tickets, etc., are sold.

words.ex: The tournament uses a knock-out system to determine the winner.
words.ex_cn: 锦标赛使用淘汰制来决定胜者。
words.en: A competition system in which the loser of each match is immediately eliminated from the competition.

words.tr: phrase. 知识经济；以知识和信息为主要生产要素的经济形态
words.ex: The country is building a knowledge economy through education and technology.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家通过教育和技术建设知识经济。
words.en: An economy based on the production, distribution, and use of knowledge and information.

words.ex: Tom often lags behind in class because he doesn't study.
words.ex_cn: 汤姆因为不学习，经常在课堂上落后。
words.en: To fail to keep up with others or to fall behind in progress, development, or achievement.

words.ex: He was laid-off due to company restructuring.
words.ex_cn: 由于公司重组，他被解雇了。
words.en: Dismissed from a job, especially temporarily because of a reduction in the workforce.

words.tr: phrase. 发射台，发射站：用于发射火箭或其他航天器的表面或结构。
words.ex: The rocket was assembled on the launch pad.
words.ex_cn: 火箭在发射台上组装完成。
words.en: A launch pad is a platform from which a rocket or missile is launched into space or the atmosphere.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.ex: The performance was criticized for extensive lip synching.
words.ex_cn: 这场表演因大量对口型而受到批评。
words.en: The act of miming to a pre-recorded song, often by a performer during a live show.

words.ex: He logs on to his computer every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上登录电脑。
words.en: To log on is to access a computer system or network by entering your username and password.

words.tr: phrase. 名人；显赫人物；有影响力的人
words.ex: He is considered a man of mark in the field of finance.
words.ex_cn: 他被认为是金融领域的名人。
words.en: A man of mark is someone who is distinguished or prominent in a particular field.

words.tr: phrase. 结婚证书（英式口语）
words.ex: He showed me his marriage lines at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他在婚礼上给我看了他的结婚证书。
words.en: A document that certifies a marriage, typically issued by a church or registry office.

words.ex: He uses a master key to open all the doors.
words.ex_cn: 他用万能钥匙打开所有门。
words.en: A master key is a key that can open many different locks.

words.ex: The old man asked for mercy killing because he was in great pain.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人因为痛苦不堪，请求安乐死。
words.en: The act of killing someone painlessly, especially someone suffering from an incurable disease; euthanasia.

words.ex: Graduating from high school was a big milestone for him.
words.ex_cn: 从高中毕业对他来说是一个重要的事件。
words.en: A milestone is a significant event or stage in the development of something.

words.tr:
adj. 多媒体的；
n. 多媒体；
words.ex: The school uses multimedia tools to teach students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校使用多媒体工具来教学。
words.en: Multimedia is the use of computers to present text, graphics, video, animation, and sound in an integrated way.

words.ex: We met at a music cafe last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚在一家音乐咖啡馆见面了。
words.en: A cafe where music, especially live music, is a regular feature, providing a relaxed atmosphere for customers to enjoy both the music and the cafe's offerings.

words.ex: The national anthem was played before the start of the game.
words.ex_cn: 比赛开始前演奏了国歌。
words.en: A national anthem is a patriotic musical composition that is officially recognized by a country's government as the state's official song.

words.tr: phrase. 储备金；为养老或应急而存的钱
words.ex: He saves money every month for his nest egg.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月存钱作为积蓄。
words.en: A nest egg is a sum of money saved for the future.

words.ex: The news agency reported the latest political developments.
words.ex_cn: 这家新闻机构报道了最新的政治发展。
words.en: A news agency is an organization that gathers news and supplies it to newspapers, magazines, television, and radio stations.

words.ex: The news briefing was canceled today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的新闻简报被取消了。
words.en: A news briefing is a meeting in which officials give information to journalists about a particular issue or event.

words.tr: phrase. 新闻发布会；记者招待会
words.ex: The president held a news conference to address the recent scandals.
words.ex_cn: 总统召开了记者招待会，以回应最近的丑闻。
words.en: A news conference is a meeting organized for the purposes of distributing information to the media and answering questions from reporters.

words.tr: phrase. 新闻快讯；突发新闻
words.ex: A news flash interrupted the regular programming.
words.ex_cn: 一条最新新闻打断了正常的节目播出。
words.en: A news flash is a brief report on an important piece of news that is given in the middle of a television or radio program.

words.tr: n. 观念；概念( notion的名词复数 )；
words.ex: Children have simple notions about right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们对对错有简单的观念。
words.en: A notion is an idea or belief about something.

words.ex: The contract was declared null and void after the fraud was discovered.
words.ex_cn: 欺诈行为被发现后，合同被宣布无效。
words.en: If something is null and void, it is considered to have no legal force or effect.

words.tr: phrase. 业余爱好；非工作时间的嗜好
words.ex: Reading is her off-hour hobby, which helps her relax after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 阅读是她的业余爱好，帮助她在一天的工作后放松。
words.en: An off-hour hobby refers to an activity that a person engages in for pleasure or relaxation during their free time, outside of their regular work or professional duties.

words.tr: phrase. 脱产培训；岗外培训；在工作场所以外进行的员工培训
words.ex: Off-the-job training allows employees to focus on learning without the daily pressures of work.
words.ex_cn: 脱产培训让员工能够在没有日常工作压力的情况下专注于学习。
words.en: Training that is provided away from the employee's usual workplace, often at a training center or educational institution.

words.tr: phrase. /adv. 待命状态；随时可用；备用
words.ex: The ambulance was on standby during the marathon.
words.ex_cn: 救护车在马拉松比赛期间处于待命状态。
words.en: If someone or something is on standby, they are ready to be used or to take action if they are needed.

words.tr: phrase. 在职培训；岗位培训；边工作边进行的培训
words.ex: He is getting on-the-job training at a car factory.
words.ex_cn: 他正在汽车工厂接受在职培训。
words.en: Training that is given to an employee at their place of work while they are doing the job.

words.tr: phrase. 现场直播；实况广播
words.ex: The news channel provided on-the-spot broadcasting of the presidential inauguration.
words.ex_cn: 新闻频道对总统就职典礼进行了现场直播。
words.en: The live transmission of an event as it happens, especially on television or radio.

words.tr: n. 严酷的考验；痛苦的经历；煎熬
words.ex: He went through a long ordeal before he found peace.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到平静之前经历了一段漫长的磨难。
words.en: An ordeal is a very unpleasant and prolonged experience.

words.ex: The car drove under the overpass.
words.ex_cn: 汽车从立交桥下开过。
words.en: An overpass is a bridge that carries one road or railway line over another.

words.ex: The overseas student lives in a dormitory.
words.ex_cn: 这位留学生住在宿舍里。
words.en: A student who comes from a foreign country to study in another country.

words.ex: The store is overstaffed during holidays.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店在节假日期间人手过多。
words.en: To provide an organization with more employees than are needed, often leading to inefficiency.

words.tr: adj. 瘫痪的；麻痹的； v. “paralyze”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The accident left him paralyzed.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故使他瘫痪了。
words.en: Unable to move or act; rendered powerless or ineffective.

words.tr: phrase. 淡化；轻描淡写；降低…的重要性
words.ex: He tried to play down his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图淡化自己的错误。
words.en: To make something seem less important or serious than it really is.

words.tr: phrase. 夸大；渲染；使…显得更重要；调皮捣蛋；出故障
words.ex: He likes to play up his successes to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢夸大自己的成功来给别人留下印象。
words.en: To emphasize or exaggerate the importance or problems of something, or to cause problems or difficulties.

words.tr: n. 入门；大门；入口网站
words.ex: This book is a portal to learning English.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是学习英语的入门。
words.en: A portal is a large and imposing entrance, doorway, or gate, or a website that provides access or links to other sites.

words.ex: The power plant makes electricity for the city.
words.ex_cn: 发电厂为城市提供电力。
words.en: A power plant is an industrial facility for the generation of electric power.

words.ex: The army took preemptive action to stop the attack.
words.ex_cn: 军队采取了先发制人的行动来阻止攻击。
words.en: A preemptive action is one that is taken in order to prevent something unpleasant from happening.

words.ex: He left school at 15, which was too premature.
words.ex_cn: 他15岁就离开了学校，这太早了。
words.en: Happening or done before the usual or expected time; not fully developed or mature.

words.tr: n. （为军队或其他组织的）采购
words.ex: The army's procurement of food and fuel takes months.
words.ex_cn: 军队的食品和燃料采购需要数月时间。
words.en: Procurement is the act of obtaining or buying goods and services, often for a business or government.

words.tr: phrase. 繁文缛节；官僚作风；繁琐的官方程序
words.ex: The project was delayed by red tape.
words.ex_cn: 该项目因官僚主义的繁文缛节而延迟。
words.en: Red tape refers to excessive regulation or rigid conformity to formal rules that is considered redundant or bureaucratic and hinders or prevents action or decision-making.

words.ex: The relevance of this topic is clear.
words.ex_cn: 这个主题的相关性是明显的。
words.en: The quality or state of being closely connected or appropriate.

words.tr:
n. 展示优点的场合（或机会）；
v. 展示…的优点；
words.ex: The competition was a showcase for her talent.
words.ex_cn: 这次比赛是她展示才华的机会。
words.en: A showcase is a setting in which someone or something is displayed to its best advantage, or a glass case used for displaying articles in a shop or museum.

words.tr:
n. 快照；
v. 突然断裂；猛然咬；
adj. 突然的；匆忙的；
words.ex: He took a snap of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他拍了一张日落的快照。
words.en: If something snaps or if you snap it, it breaks suddenly, usually with a sharp cracking noise. | A snap is a photograph. | If someone snaps, or if something snaps inside them, they suddenly stop being calm and become very angry.

words.tr: phrase. 快速民意调查；突击民调（指短时间内进行的非正式投票或调查，用以快速了解公众意见）
words.ex: The news channel conducted a snap poll to gauge public reaction to the recent policy announcement.
words.ex_cn: 新闻频道进行了一次即时民意调查，以了解公众对最近政策公告的反应。
words.en: A snap poll is an opinion poll conducted quickly, often in response to a sudden event or to gauge immediate public reaction to a specific issue.

words.tr: phrase. 声音探测设备；用于侦测声音的装置
words.ex: The researchers used sound-detection gear to study the communication patterns of dolphins.
words.ex_cn: 研究人员使用声音检测设备来研究海豚的交流模式。
words.en: Equipment used for detecting sounds, often employed in scientific research, wildlife monitoring, or security.

words.ex: He gets too much spam in his email.
words.ex_cn: 他的邮箱里收到了太多垃圾邮件。
words.en: Unsolicited messages, especially advertisements, sent in large quantities on the internet.

words.ex: He bought a stake in the new company.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了这家新公司的股份。
words.en: A stake is a pointed stick or post that is pushed into the ground, for example to support a young tree. It can also refer to a share or interest in a business, situation, or system.

words.ex: Stem cells have the potential to differentiate into various types of cells.
words.ex_cn: 干细胞有分化成多种类型细胞的潜力。
words.en: A stem cell is a type of cell that has the ability to develop into any type of cell in the body, making them a focus of research in regenerative medicine.

words.ex: He will step down from the stage after the speech.
words.ex_cn: 演讲结束后，他会走下舞台。
words.en: To resign from a position or to reduce the intensity, amount, or level of something.

words.ex: The strike caused a stoppage of the train service.
words.ex_cn: 罢工导致了列车服务的停止。
words.en: A stoppage is an instance of stopping or the state of being stopped, especially in a work context.

words.tr:
v. 痛哭；嚎啕；尖叫
n. 痛哭；哀号；尖啸
words.ex: The baby wails when she is hungry.
words.ex_cn: 当宝宝饿的时候，她会哭喊。
words.en: To wail means to make a long, high cry, usually because you are in pain or very sad.

chapters.name: 主题分类词汇 政治、法律类

words.tr: phrase. 一揽子提议；一系列建议
words.ex: The government introduced a package of proposals aimed at reducing carbon emissions.
words.ex_cn: 政府提出了一组旨在减少碳排放的提案。
words.en: A set of proposals offered or considered as a whole.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: He was absent from school yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天缺席了学校。
words.en: If someone or something is absent from a place or situation where they should be or where they usually are, they are not there.

words.tr: phrase. 缺席投票（指选民在无法亲自到场的情况下通过邮寄或其他方式投票）
words.ex: He applied for absent voting because he would be out of town on election day.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了缺席投票，因为选举日他会在城外。
words.en: Absent voting refers to the process of voting by those who are unable to attend their designated polling place on election day.

words.tr: phrase. 绝对多数；超过半数的票数或支持
words.ex: The party won an absolute majority in the parliament.
words.ex_cn: 该党在议会中赢得了绝对多数。
words.en: An absolute majority is more than half of the votes or seats in a decision-making body, such as a parliament or council.

words.tr: phrase. v. 避免投票；弃权
words.ex: He will abstain from voting because he disagrees with both candidates.
words.ex_cn: 他将弃权，因为他不同意这两个候选人。
words.en: To deliberately refrain from participating in a formal vote or election process.

words.tr: phrase. 赞成票；表示同意的投票
words.ex: The bill passed with a majority of affirmative votes.
words.ex_cn: n. 法案以多数赞成票通过。
words.en: An affirmative vote is a vote that supports a proposal or candidate in a formal decision-making process.

words.tr: phrase. 同盟国（尤指第一次或第二次世界大战中联合对抗轴心国的国家）
words.ex: During World War II, the Allied Powers fought against the Axis Powers.
words.ex_cn: 在第二次世界大战期间，同盟国与轴心国作战。
words.en: The Allied Powers were the countries that opposed the Axis Powers during World War II, including the United States, the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union, and others.

words.tr: phrase. 彻底的禁令；全面禁止的
words.ex: The government imposed an all-out ban on cigarette sales to minors.
words.ex_cn: 政府对未成年人实施了全面禁止销售香烟的禁令。
words.en: An all-out ban is a complete prohibition of something, leaving no exceptions or loopholes.

words.ex: He is an ambassador to France.
words.ex_cn: 他是驻法国的大使。
words.en: An ambassador is an official envoy, especially a high-ranking diplomat who represents a state and is usually accredited to another sovereign state or to an international organization as the resident representative of their own government or sovereign or appointed for a special and often temporary diplomatic assignment.

words.ex: The amendment changed the old law.
words.ex_cn: 这项修正案改变了旧法律。
words.en: An amendment is a change or addition to a law or document.

words.ex: They had an amicable talk after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 争吵之后，他们进行了一次友好的交谈。
words.en: When people have an amicable relationship, they are pleasant towards each other and solve their problems without arguing.

words.ex: The government gave amnesty to political prisoners.
words.ex_cn: 政府向政治犯提供了赦免。
words.en: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of people by a government, especially for political offenses.

words.ex: The country fell into anarchy after the war.
words.ex_cn: 战争之后，这个国家陷入了混乱。
words.en: Anarchy is a state of disorder due to absence or nonrecognition of authority or other controlling systems.

words.ex: The school made an announcement about the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 学校发布了关于假期的通告。
words.en: A public or formal notice about something that has happened or is going to happen.

words.tr: n. （以往南非的）种族隔离制度
words.ex: He lived under apartheid in South Africa.
words.ex_cn: 他在南非生活在种族隔离制度下。
words.en: A policy or system of segregation or discrimination on grounds of race, especially the policy that was in place in South Africa from 1948 to 1994.

words.tr:
n. 吸引力；上诉；
v. 吸引；诉请；呼吁；
words.ex: The appeal of the beach drew many tourists.
words.ex_cn: 海滩的吸引力吸引了许多游客。
words.en: If you appeal to someone to do something, you make a serious and urgent request to them. If you appeal against a decision or sentence, you formally ask a court or other authority to change it. If something appeals to you, you like it or it interests you.

words.ex: The hero in the story is an archetype of courage.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的英雄是勇气的原型。
words.en: An archetype is a very typical example of a certain person or thing.

words.tr: phrase. 武装干涉；军事干预
words.ex: The United Nations debated the necessity of armed intervention in the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 联合国就冲突中武装干预的必要性进行了辩论。
words.en: Armed intervention refers to the use of military force by one or more countries in the affairs of another country, typically to achieve a specific political or military objective.

words.ex: He had to resort to arm-twisting to get his colleagues to agree.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不采取施压手段让同事们同意。
words.en: The act of persuading someone to do something by using strong or forceful methods.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.ex: The man was arrested for arson.
words.ex_cn: 这名男子因纵火被逮捕。
words.en: The crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

words.tr: n. 收容所；避难所；精神病院；（政治）庇护
words.ex: The old building now serves as an asylum for the homeless.
words.ex_cn: 这栋旧建筑现在是无家可归者的收容所。
words.en: An asylum is a place where people who are in danger or who have no homes can go for safety and protection.

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.tr: phrase. 选票；投票用的纸张
words.ex: Voters cast their votes by marking the ballot paper.
words.ex_cn: 选民通过在选票上标记来投票。
words.en: A ballot paper is a piece of paper on which you indicate your choice or opinion in a secret vote.

words.tr: phrase. 双边贸易；两国之间的贸易往来
words.ex: Bilateral trade agreements are important for fostering economic cooperation between countries.
words.ex_cn: 双边贸易协定对于促进国家间的经济合作至关重要。
words.en: Trade between two countries or regions.

words.ex: I paid the electric bill yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天付了电费账单。
words.en: A bill is a statement of money owed for goods or services, a proposed law presented to a legislature for approval, a piece of paper money, or the beak of a bird.

words.tr: phrase. 覆盖性投票；全体投票（指涵盖所有候选人或选项的投票方式）
words.ex: The state implemented a blanket ballot to ensure all residents could vote on the same issues.
words.ex_cn: 该州实施了全面选举，以确保所有居民都能对相同的问题进行投票。
words.en: A ballot that includes all candidates or issues in a single vote, allowing voters to make a comprehensive choice.

words.ex: The soldiers were bombarded with cannon fire.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们遭到炮火轰击。
words.en: To bombard someone or something means to attack them continuously with bombs, shells, or other missiles. It can also mean to subject someone to a lot of something, such as questions or information.

words.ex: The river forms the border between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 这条河是两个国家的边界。
words.en: The edge or boundary of something, or the part near it; a dividing line.

words.ex: The toy will break apart if you pull it hard.
words.ex_cn: 如果你用力拉，玩具会散开。
words.en: To separate into parts or pieces, often suddenly or violently.

words.ex: He believes in capitalism and owns a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他相信资本主义，并拥有一家小企业。
words.en: Capitalism is an economic system in which the means of production are privately owned and operated for profit in a competitive market.

words.tr: n. 政党会议；核心小组会议；特别利益集团
words.ex: The caucus decided on a new strategy for the upcoming election.
words.ex_cn: 党团会议决定了一项新的选举策略。
words.en: A caucus is a meeting of the members of a political party to select candidates or decide policy.

words.tr:
v. 声称；索赔；
n. 声称；索要；
words.ex: He claims that he saw a UFO last night.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己昨晚看到了不明飞行物。
words.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.tr: n. 群体；殖民地；聚居地；
words.ex: A colony of ants moved quickly across the ground.
words.ex_cn: 一群蚂蚁迅速从地上爬过。
words.en: A colony is a country or area that is under the political control of another country, usually one that is far away, and where people from that country live.

words.tr: n. 联邦；共和国；联合体；
words.ex: Australia is a member of the Commonwealth.
words.ex_cn: 澳大利亚是联邦的成员。
words.en: A commonwealth is a traditional English term for a political community founded for the common good. Historically, it has been synonymous with 'republic'.

words.ex: He filed a complaint about the noisy neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他投诉了吵闹的邻居。
words.en: A complaint is a statement in which you express your dissatisfaction with a particular situation.

words.ex: The states formed a confederation to share power.
words.ex_cn: 这些州组成了一个联盟来分享权力。
words.en: A confederation is an organization which consists of a number of parties or groups united in an alliance.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: The politician lost his constituency after the scandal.
words.ex_cn: 这位政客在丑闻后失去了他的支持者。
words.en: A constituency is a group of people in a country or area who are entitled to vote in an election, or the area itself.

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: He went to the consulate to get a visa.
words.ex_cn: 他去领事馆办理签证。
words.en: A consulate is the place where a consul works, which is an official who is sent by their country to live in a foreign city in order to help other citizens from their own country and to represent their country's commercial interests.

words.ex: He had a consultation with the doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他与医生进行了一次咨询。
words.en: A consultation is a meeting which is held to discuss something. Consultation is discussion about something that is still being planned.

words.tr:
v. 定罪；宣判有罪
n. 罪犯；囚犯
words.ex: The court convicted him of theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院判定他犯有盗窃罪。
words.en: If someone is convicted of a crime, they are found guilty of that crime in a court of law.

words.tr: phrase. 政变策划者；参与策划政变的人
words.ex: The coup plotter was arrested before the plan could be executed.
words.ex_cn: 政变策划者在计划执行前被逮捕。
words.en: A coup plotter is someone who plans or organizes a coup, which is a sudden, violent, and illegal seizure of power from a government.

words.ex: The government started a crackdown on illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 政府开始对非法毒品进行严厉打击。
words.en: A crackdown is a series of severe measures taken to restrict or suppress undesirable or illegal people or behavior.

words.ex: The police caught the man for a serious crime.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓住了那个犯下严重罪行的人。
words.en: A crime is an illegal action or activity for which a person can be punished by law.

words.tr:
v. 辩论；争论
n. 辩论；争论
words.ex: The students had a debate about homework.
words.ex_cn: 学生们就作业进行了一场辩论。
words.en: A debate is a discussion about a subject on which people have different views.

words.tr: n. 外交官；会耍手腕儿的人
words.ex: The diplomat met the president yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 这位外交官昨天会见了总统。
words.en: A diplomat is a person who represents their country in a foreign country, managing political relations and negotiations.

words.tr: phrase. 外交途径；通过正式外交途径进行的沟通或交涉
words.ex: The two countries resolved their conflict through diplomatic channels.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家通过外交途径解决了他们的冲突。
words.en: Diplomatic channels refer to the official routes or methods used by governments to communicate with each other, especially in matters of international relations.

words.tr: phrase. 外交信使；负责传递外交文件或物品的官方人员
words.ex: The diplomatic courier was entrusted with sensitive documents.
words.ex_cn: 这位外交信使被托付携带敏感文件。
words.en: A diplomatic courier is an official who is responsible for the secure transportation of diplomatic mail between embassies, consulates, and other diplomatic missions.

words.tr: phrase. 外交豁免权；外交人员享有的免于驻在国法律管辖的特权
words.ex: Diplomatic immunities are granted to protect foreign diplomats.
words.ex_cn: 外交豁免权是为了保护外交官而授予的。
words.en: Diplomatic immunities are exemptions from certain laws and taxes granted to diplomats by the country in which they are posted to ensure they can perform their duties without interference.

words.tr: phrase. 外交特权；外交豁免权
words.ex: Diplomatic privileges allow diplomats to enjoy certain immunities.
words.ex_cn: 外交特权使外交官享有某些豁免权。
words.en: Diplomatic privileges refer to the rights and immunities granted to diplomats and their families in a foreign country, enabling them to perform their duties without interference from the host country.

words.tr: phrase. 外交等级；外交官的级别
words.ex: He was promoted to the diplomatic rank of ambassador.
words.ex_cn: 他被提升为大使的外交官衔。
words.en: The position or status of a diplomat, indicating their level of authority and responsibility in the diplomatic service.

words.ex: The room was in complete disorder.
words.ex_cn: 房间一片混乱。
words.en: A disorder is a state of confusion or untidiness, or a medical problem that affects the mind or body.

words.ex: Please don't disturb me while I'm reading.
words.ex_cn: 我读书时请不要打扰我。
words.en: To disturb someone means to interrupt what they are doing and cause them inconvenience or annoyance.

words.tr: adj. 引起烦恼的；令人不安的； v. 打扰；妨碍；“disturb”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie showed a disturbing scene of violence.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一个引起烦恼的暴力场景。
words.en: If you describe something as disturbing, you mean that it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.ex: He wrote a draft of the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送之前写了这封信的草稿。
words.en: A draft is a preliminary version of a piece of writing, or a current of air in a room or other confined space. It can also refer to the act of selecting someone for a particular purpose or task, especially in sports or the military.

words.tr: phrase. 在某人不在期间；在某人缺席的时候
words.ex: He took care of my dog during my absence.
words.ex_cn: 我不在的时候，他帮我照看我的狗。
words.en: Throughout the period when someone is not present.

words.ex: The proposed law aims to criminalize ecocide.
words.ex_cn: 这项拟议的法律旨在将生态灭绝定为犯罪。
words.en: Ecocide refers to the extensive damage to, destruction of, or loss of ecosystem(s) of a given territory, whether by human agency or by other causes, to such an extent that peaceful enjoyment by the inhabitants of that territory has been severely diminished.

words.tr: phrase. 经济实力；经济力量
words.ex: The country's economic power has grown significantly over the past decade.
words.ex_cn: n. 该国的经济力量在过去十年中显著增长。
words.en: Economic power refers to the capacity of a country, individual, or organization to influence economic conditions and outcomes.

words.ex: The election will be held next month.
words.ex_cn: 选举将在下个月举行。
words.en: An election is a process in which people vote to choose a person or group of people to hold an official position.

words.tr: n. 挑选者；选拔者；选择器
words.ex: The selector can filter items based on specific criteria.
words.ex_cn: 选择器可以根据特定标准筛选项目。
words.en: A selector is someone who chooses or selects, especially someone whose job is to choose people or things for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He went to the embassy to get a visa.
words.ex_cn: 他去大使馆办理签证。
words.en: An embassy is a group of officials who represent their country in a foreign country, or the building where they work.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.ex: The police found evidence at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了证据。
words.en: Evidence is anything that you see, experience, read, or are told that causes you to believe that something is true or has really happened.

words.ex: The doctor did an examination of his arm.
words.ex_cn: 医生对他手臂进行了检查。
words.en: An examination is a formal test that you take to show your knowledge or ability in a particular subject, or to obtain a qualification.

words.tr:
adj. 很好的；晴朗的；健康的；
n. 罚款；
words.ex: She did a fine job on the project.
words.ex_cn: 她在这个项目上做得很好。
words.en: If you say that something is fine, you mean that it is satisfactory or acceptable.

words.tr: phrase. 外交事务；对外关系
words.ex: He dedicated his life to foreign affairs and international diplomacy.
words.ex_cn: 他一生致力于外交事务和国际外交。
words.en: Matters concerning the relations between countries, especially in diplomacy and international relations.

words.tr: phrase. 友好的交流；友善的往来
words.ex: The two countries have established friendly exchanges in the field of education.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家在教育领域建立了友好交流。
words.en: Friendly exchanges refer to the amicable interactions or communications between individuals, groups, or nations, often aimed at fostering goodwill and mutual understanding.

words.ex: The king governed the land for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 国王统治这个国家50年。
words.en: To govern a country or an organization means to officially control and manage its affairs.

words.ex: The governmental office closed early on Friday.
words.ex_cn: 政府办公室星期五提早关门。
words.en: Relating to the government or the public affairs of a country.

words.tr: pron. 他们的；她们的；它们的；
words.ex: Their books are on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他们的书在桌子上。
words.en: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.

words.ex: The police opened an inquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An inquiry is a question which you ask in order to get some information.

words.tr: phrase. 国际形势；国际局势
words.ex: The international situation is constantly changing due to various global events.
words.ex_cn: 由于各种全球事件，国际形势不断变化。
words.en: The global political and economic environment, especially as it affects the relations between nations.

words.tr: phrase. 国际水域；公海（指不属于任何国家主权管辖的海域）
words.ex: The ship sailed into international waters to avoid legal repercussions.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船驶入国际水域以避免法律后果。
words.en: The parts of the ocean that are not under the jurisdiction of any country.

words.tr:
n. 法官；裁判；
v. 判断；评判；
words.ex: The judge announced the verdict in court.
words.ex_cn: 法官在法庭上宣布了判决。
words.en: A judge is a person who has the authority to decide questions brought before a court of law. To judge means to form an opinion or conclusion about something.

words.ex: The jury decided the man was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团裁定这个人无罪。
words.en: A jury is a group of people who are chosen to decide whether someone is guilty or not guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: The judge made a fair decision to show justice.
words.ex_cn: 法官做出了公正的裁决以体现公正。
words.en: Justice is fairness in the way that people are treated.

words.ex: The lawyer helps people with legal problems.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助人们解决法律问题。
words.en: A lawyer is a person who is qualified to advise people about the law and represent them in court.

words.ex: He hired a legal lawyer to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一位法律律师来帮助他。
words.en: Relating to the law or to lawyers, or permitted or required by law.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.tr:
adj. 开明的；自由主义的；
n. 自由党党员；
words.ex: He is a liberal teacher who listens to students.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位开明的老师，会倾听学生的声音。
words.en: A liberal person, system, or policy is one that is in favour of allowing people a lot of freedom in their behaviour or opinions.

words.tr: phrase. 海洋资源；海事资源
words.ex: The country is exploring its maritime resources to boost its economy.
words.ex_cn: 该国正在探索其海洋资源以提振经济。
words.en: Maritime resources refer to the natural resources found in the ocean, including fish, minerals, and energy sources.

words.tr: phrase. 国家的合并；州际合并；邦联合并
words.ex: The merger of states created a new country.
words.ex_cn: 国家的合并诞生了一个新的国家。
words.en: The political or administrative unification of multiple independent states into a single governing entity.

words.ex: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs handles international relations.
words.ex_cn: 外交部处理国际关系。
words.en: The government department responsible for the conduct of a country's foreign relations.

words.ex: The country still has a monarchy with a king as the head of state.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家仍然实行君主制，国王是国家元首。
words.en: A monarchy is a form of government in which a country is ruled by a monarch, such as a king or queen.

words.ex: The murder happened last night in the park.
words.ex_cn: 这起谋杀发生在昨晚的公园里。
words.en: Murder is the unlawful premeditated killing of one human being by another.

words.tr: phrase. 相互承认；互认（指双方或多方彼此正式接受对方的资格、标准或法律地位）
words.ex: The agreement on mutual recognition has facilitated trade between the two countries.
words.ex_cn: 相互认可协议促进了两国之间的贸易。
words.en: Mutual recognition refers to the agreement between two or more parties to accept and acknowledge each other's standards, qualifications, or judgments.

words.ex: The motion was defeated by a negative vote.
words.ex_cn: 该动议因反对票而被否决。
words.en: A vote indicating opposition to a proposal or motion.

words.ex: He kept neutrality during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: The state of not supporting or helping either side in a conflict, disagreement, etc.; impartiality.

words.ex: He is the nominee for best actor.
words.ex_cn: 他是最佳男演员的提名人。
words.en: A nominee is someone who is proposed for an official position or for an honour or award.

words.ex: The teacher did normalization of the test scores.
words.ex_cn: 老师对考试成绩进行了正常化。
words.en: The process of making something normal or standard, especially in the context of social or political relations.

words.tr: phrase. 民意调查；民意测验；舆论调查
words.ex: The newspaper did an opinion poll about the election.
words.ex_cn: 报纸就选举做了一项民意调查。
words.en: An opinion poll is a survey of public opinion from a particular sample.

words.tr: phrase. 破坏和平者；蓄意阻挠和平进程的人
words.ex: The peace saboteurs aimed to disrupt the peace talks.
words.ex_cn: 这些和平破坏者的目的是破坏和平谈判。
words.en: A person who deliberately destroys or obstructs something, especially for political or military advantage, specifically in the context of peace efforts.

words.ex: He got a penalty for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规则而受到惩罚。
words.en: A penalty is a punishment that is imposed on someone for doing something that is against the rules or the law.

words.tr: phrase. 常任成员；常任理事国（尤指联合国安理会五个常任理事国）
words.ex: China is one of the permanent members of the UN Security Council.
words.ex_cn: 中国是联合国安理会的常任理事国之一。
words.en: A permanent member is a member of an organization, especially the United Nations Security Council, who holds their position indefinitely without the need for re-election.

words.tr:
n. 力量；电源；权力；强国；
v. 给…提供能量；供以动力；
words.ex: The power of the storm broke the trees.
words.ex_cn: 风暴的力量折断了树木。
words.en: The ability or capacity to do something or act in a particular way; control or influence over others; electrical energy supplied to a device or building.

words.tr: phrase. 权力斗争；权力争夺
words.ex: The company has been embroiled in a power struggle since the CEO's unexpected resignation.
words.ex_cn: 自从CEO意外辞职后，公司就一直深陷权力斗争之中。
words.en: A power struggle is a situation in which two or more people or groups are competing for control in a particular organization or country.

words.tr: adj. 首要的；小学的；初等的；原来的；最初的；
words.ex: Primary goal is to stay safe.
words.ex_cn: 首要目标是保持安全。
words.en: Something that is primary is more important than anything else.

words.ex: He was sent to prison for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窃被送进了监狱。
words.en: A prison is a building where criminals are kept as punishment or where people accused of a crime are kept before their trial.

words.ex: The prisoner walked in the yard every day.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯每天在院子里散步。
words.en: A prisoner is a person who is kept in a prison as a punishment for a crime they have committed or while awaiting trial.

words.ex: The math teacher asked for a proof of the theorem.
words.ex_cn: 数学老师要求给出这个定理的证明。
words.en: Proof is a fact, argument, or piece of evidence which shows that something is definitely true or definitely exists.

words.tr: n. 保护国；摄政政体；摄政职位；摄政任期
words.ex: The country became a protectorate of the neighboring empire.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家成为了邻近帝国的保护国。
words.en: A protectorate is a state that is controlled and protected by another.

words.tr: phrase. 抗议票（为表达对主要候选人或政策不满而投给非主流候选人的选票）
words.ex: A protest vote is often cast to express dissatisfaction with the candidates.
words.ex_cn: 反对票通常是为了表达对候选人的不满而投的。
words.en: A protest vote is a vote cast in an election to demonstrate dissatisfaction with the choice of candidates or the current political system.

words.ex: The queen's reign lasted 70 years.
words.ex_cn: 女王的统治持续了70年。
words.en: The period during which a sovereign rules; to hold royal office; to prevail

words.tr: phrase. 难民营；收容难民的临时营地
words.ex: The refugee camp was overcrowded and lacked basic amenities.
words.ex_cn: 难民营人满为患，缺乏基本设施。
words.en: A refugee camp is a temporary settlement built to receive refugees.

words.ex: France is a republic with a president.
words.ex_cn: 法国是一个有总统的共和国。
words.en: A republic is a country where power is held by the people or their elected representatives, and which has an elected or nominated president rather than a monarch.

words.ex: The French Revolution changed the government.
words.ex_cn: 法国大革命改变了政府。
words.en: A revolution is a sudden, extreme, or complete change in something, or the act of making such a change.

words.ex: The ruler made laws for his people.
words.ex_cn: 这位统治者为他的人民制定法律。
words.en: A ruler is a person who governs or commands. It can also refer to a straight strip or cylinder of plastic, wood, metal, or other rigid material, typically marked at regular intervals and used to draw straight lines or measure distances.

words.ex: This sentence is easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这个句子很容易理解。
words.en: A sentence is a group of words which, when they are written down, begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark. Most sentences contain a subject and a verb.

words.tr: n. 定居点；定居（过程）；协议；
words.ex: The small settlement near the river has five houses.
words.ex_cn: 河边的小定居点有五所房子。
words.en: A settlement is an official agreement intended to resolve a dispute or conflict.

words.ex: He believes in socialism and wants equal rights for all.
words.ex_cn: 他相信社会主义，希望所有人都享有平等的权利。
words.en: Socialism is a political and economic theory of social organization which advocates that the means of production, distribution, and exchange should be owned or regulated by the community as a whole.

words.ex: The country values its sovereignty.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家重视它的主权。
words.en: Sovereignty is the power that a country has to govern itself or another country or state.

words.ex: The company made a statement about the new policy.
words.ex_cn: 公司就新政策发布了一项声明。
words.en: A statement is something that you say or write which gives information in a formal or definite way.

words.tr: phrase. 国事访问；国家元首或政府首脑应他国邀请进行的正式访问
words.ex: The president made a state visit to China to discuss trade agreements.
words.ex_cn: 总统对中国进行了国事访问，以讨论贸易协议。
words.en: A state visit is a formal visit by a head of state to another country, at the invitation of that country's government, which is usually characterized by a series of official ceremonies and events.

words.ex: He will sue the company for damages.
words.ex_cn: 他将起诉这家公司要求赔偿。
words.en: To sue means to start a legal case against someone, usually to claim money from them because they have caused you harm or loss.

words.tr: n. 投票；选举权；参政权
words.ex: Women won suffrage in 1920.
words.ex_cn: 女性在1920年获得了选举权。
words.en: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.

words.tr: phrase. 合作；组队；联手（通常指为了共同目标而与他人协作）
words.ex: They team up to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: To join together with someone in order to work on something as a team.

words.tr: phrase. 领空；一国主权管辖范围内的空中区域
words.ex: The violation of territorial air is a serious international issue.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯领空是一个严重的国际问题。
words.en: The airspace above a nation's territory, over which the nation claims sovereignty.

words.tr: phrase. 领海；一国主权管辖下的邻接其陆地领土及内水的一定宽度的海域
words.ex: The country controls its territorial sea up to 12 nautical miles.
words.ex_cn: 该国对其领海拥有控制权，范围达12海里。
words.en: The territorial sea is a belt of coastal waters extending at most 12 nautical miles from the baseline of a coastal state. The territorial sea is regarded as the sovereign territory of the state, although foreign ships (both military and civilian) are allowed innocent passage through it; this sovereignty also extends to the airspace over and seabed below.

words.tr: phrase. 领海；一国主权管辖下的邻接其陆地领土及内水的一定宽度的海域
words.ex: The boat stayed inside the country's territorial waters.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船停留在该国的领海内。
words.en: The waters under the jurisdiction of a state, especially the part of the sea within a stated distance of the shore.

words.ex: The country expanded its territory after the war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在战争后扩大了它的领土。
words.en: An area of land that is controlled by a particular country, ruler, or military force.

words.ex: The theft of the bike was reported to the police.
words.ex_cn: 这起自行车被盗事件已向警方报告。
words.en: Theft is the act of stealing.

words.tr: phrase. 输掉选举；在选举中落败
words.ex: He worked hard, but he still lost the election.
words.ex_cn: 他努力了，但还是输掉了选举。
words.en: To fail to win an election.

words.tr: phrase. 赢得选举；在选举中获胜
words.ex: He wants to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 他想赢得选举。
words.en: To achieve victory in a political election, securing the required majority of votes.

words.ex: The doctor ran a trial to test the new medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了试验来测试这种新药。
words.en: A trial is a formal meeting in a law court, at which a judge and jury listen to evidence and decide whether a person is guilty of a crime.

words.tr: v. （使）统一；（使）联合；（使）成一体；
words.ex: The two teams decided to unify their efforts.
words.ex_cn: 这两个团队决定统一他们的努力。
words.en: To unify means to make or become united, uniform, or whole.

words.ex: The two teams decide to unite for the competition.
words.ex_cn: 这两个队伍决定在比赛中联合起来。
words.en: If a group of people or things unite or if someone unites them, they join together and act as a group.

words.tr: n. 投票者；选民；选举人
words.ex: The voter cast his ballot in the election.
words.ex_cn: 这位选民在选举中投了票。
words.en: A voter is a person who votes or has the right to vote in an election.

words.ex: He will vote for the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 他将投票支持新领袖。
words.en: If you vote, you indicate your choice officially at a meeting or in an election, for example by raising your hand or writing on a piece of paper.

words.tr:
auxv. 将会；愿意；
n. 意志；意愿；遗嘱；
words.ex: I will go to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天会去公园。
words.en: The word 'will' can be used as a noun to refer to the faculty by which a person decides on and initiates action, or as a verb to indicate a desire or intention to do something.

chapters.name: 主题分类词汇 经济类

words.tr:
n. 账户；叙述；账目；
v. 占…；说明；
words.ex: I opened a bank account last week.
words.ex_cn: 我上周开了一家银行账户。
words.en: An account is a detailed report or description of an event or situation.

words.tr: phrase. 账户结算；账目清算
words.ex: They finished the account settlement last week.
words.ex_cn: 他们上周完成了账目结算。
words.en: The process of reconciling the transactions in an account to determine the final balance, often involving the payment of outstanding amounts.

words.ex: The company has an accumulated deficit of $500,000.
words.ex_cn: 该公司累计亏损50万美元。
words.en: An accumulated deficit is the total net loss that a company or government has incurred over time, often resulting from spending more than it earns.

words.tr: phrase. 主动贸易顺差；指一国在对外贸易中出口额持续大于进口额的状况
words.ex: The country's active trade balance has been growing steadily.
words.ex_cn: 该国的贸易顺差一直在稳步增长。
words.en: A situation where the value of a country's exports exceeds the value of its imports.

words.ex: The teacher will assess your homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会评估你的作业。
words.en: to judge or decide the amount, value, quality, or importance of something

words.tr: phrase. 汽车贷款；用于购买汽车的贷款
words.ex: He got an auto loan to buy a used car.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔汽车贷款来买一辆二手车。
words.en: An auto loan is a sum of money borrowed from a bank or other financial institution to purchase a car, which is then paid back over time with interest.

words.tr:
n. 保释（金）
v. 保释；（往外）舀水
words.ex: He paid bail to get out of jail.
words.ex_cn: 他交了保释金以便出狱。
words.en: Bail is a sum of money that a person who has been accused of a crime pays to a law court so that they can be released until their trial. The payment is a way of making sure that the accused will return to court for trial.

words.ex: He checks his bank book every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都会查看他的存折。
words.en: A bank book is a small book in which a bank customer's transactions are recorded.

words.tr: phrase. 银行倒闭；银行破产
words.ex: The bank failure caused a panic among investors.
words.ex_cn: 银行破产引发了投资者的恐慌。
words.en: The collapse of a bank due to its inability to meet its financial obligations.

words.ex: He scans the barcode with a small machine.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个小机器扫描条形码。
words.en: A bar code is a pattern of thick and thin black lines that is printed on things you buy. It contains information that a computer can read.

words.tr: phrase. 特价；便宜的价格；划算的价钱
words.ex: I got this jacket at a bargain price during the sale.
words.ex_cn: 我在促销期间以特价买了这件夹克。
words.en: A bargain price refers to a price that is lower than usual or expected, often considered a good deal.

words.ex: He was late due to traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他因为交通堵塞迟到了。
words.en: If an event is due to something, it happens or exists as a direct result of that thing.

words.tr: be scheduled to 预定要；安排要（做某事）
words.ex: The meeting is scheduled to start at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 会议定于上午9点开始。
words.en: If something is scheduled to happen at a particular time, arrangements are made for it to happen at that time.

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

words.ex: The city had an economic boom after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市迎来了经济繁荣。
words.en: If there is a boom in the economy, there is an increase in economic activity, for example in the amount of things that are being bought and sold.

words.tr: phrase. + n. 推动基础设施建设；促进基础设施发展
words.ex: The government will boost infrastructure to create more jobs.
words.ex_cn: 政府将加强基础设施建设以创造更多就业机会。
words.en: To enhance or develop physical and organizational structures, such as roads, bridges, or digital networks, to improve efficiency and capacity.

words.tr: phrase. 打破禁忌；挑战传统禁忌观念
words.ex: Artists try to break taboos and talk about things people avoid.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家试图打破禁忌，谈论人们回避的话题。
words.en: To do something that is considered forbidden or socially unacceptable.

words.ex: He brokered a deal between the two companies.
words.ex_cn: 他为两家公司安排了协商并达成协议。
words.en: A broker is a person whose job is to buy and sell shares, foreign money, or goods for other people.

words.tr: phrase. 预算削减；财政紧缩
words.ex: The school faced a budget cut this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年学校遇到了预算削减。
words.en: A reduction in the amount of money allocated to a particular purpose or project, typically as part of an effort to reduce overall spending.

words.tr: phrase. 商业萧条；经济衰退期；生意低迷期
words.ex: The company is experiencing a business slump due to the economic downturn.
words.ex_cn: 由于经济衰退，该公司正经历营业不振。
words.en: A business slump refers to a significant decline in business activity or economic conditions.

words.tr: phrase. 资本外流；指资金从一个国家流向其他国家的现象
words.ex: The country is facing big capital outflow.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正面临大量资本外流。
words.en: The movement of capital out of a country, especially when it is invested abroad.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏现金的；没有资本的
words.ex: The cash-strapped family could not buy new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 这个资金紧张的家庭买不起新鞋。
words.en: If a person or organization is cash-strapped, they do not have enough money to buy or pay for the things they want or need.

words.ex: Blood circulates in the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液在体内循环。
words.en: To move or cause to move continuously or freely through a closed system or area.

words.tr: phrase. 货币兑换器；汇率换算工具
words.ex: He uses a currency converter to change dollars to euros.
words.ex_cn: 他使用货币兑换器将美元换成欧元。
words.en: A currency converter is a tool that allows you to calculate the value of one currency in terms of another.

words.tr: phrase. 裁员；减少员工数量
words.ex: The company will cut down the staff to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司将裁员以节省开支。
words.en: To reduce the number of employees in a company or organization, typically to save money or because there is less work to do.

words.ex: He felt deep depression after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到深深的抑郁。
words.en: A period during which business, employment, and stock-market values decline severely or remain at a very low level of activity.

words.ex: The government announced a devaluation of the currency.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布货币贬值。
words.en: A reduction in the value of a currency with respect to other monetary units.

words.tr: n. 被除数；股份红利；股息
words.ex: In 12 ÷ 3 = 4, the dividend is 12.
words.en: A dividend is a sum of money paid regularly (typically annually) by a company to its shareholders out of its profits (or reserves).

words.tr: phrase. 市场不景气的；交易清淡的
words.ex: The dull market is characterized by low trading volumes and minimal price fluctuations.
words.ex_cn: 市面冷淡的特点是交易量低，价格波动小。
words.en: A market characterized by low trading volume and little price movement, making it difficult for traders to make profits.

words.ex: The country faced economic contraction last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个国家经历了经济收缩。
words.en: A period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced, generally identified by a fall in GDP in two successive quarters.

words.tr: phrase. 经济衰退；指一个国家的经济活动显著下降，通常表现为GDP连续两个季度负增长
words.ex: The country faced an economic recession last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个国家经历了经济衰退。
words.en: A period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced, generally identified by a fall in GDP in two successive quarters.

words.tr: phrase. 经济起飞，指一个国家或地区经济开始迅速增长并进入持续发展的阶段
words.ex: China's economic take-off began in the late 1970s.
words.ex_cn: 中国的经济起飞始于20世纪70年代末。
words.en: A period of rapid economic growth and development.

words.tr: phrase. 经济刺激；指政府为促进经济增长而采取的财政或货币政策措施
words.ex: The government gave an economic stimulus to help businesses.
words.ex_cn: 政府提供了经济刺激以帮助企业。
words.en: An economic stimulus is a set of measures taken by a government to stimulate a flagging economy, often involving increased public spending and tax cuts.

words.tr: phrase. 过剩劳动力；多余的劳工
words.ex: The factory has excess labor this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个工厂这个月有多余的劳动力。
words.en: Excess labor refers to a situation where there are more workers available than there are jobs for them to fill, leading to unemployment or underemployment.

words.tr: phrase. 以出口为导向的产业；主要为出口市场生产商品的工业部门
words.ex: The country supports export-oriented industries to earn foreign money.
words.ex_cn: 该国支持出口导向型产业以赚取外汇。
words.en: Industries that focus on producing goods for export rather than for domestic consumption.

words.ex: The country has a large financial deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家有巨大的财政赤字。
words.en: A situation where a government, company, or individual spends more money than they receive in a particular period, resulting in a shortfall.

words.tr: phrase. 数十年来；几十年间
words.ex: He has worked as a teacher for decades.
words.ex_cn: 他几十年来一直当老师。
words.en: For a long period of many years.

words.tr: phrase. 金本位制；黄金标准（指衡量事物的最高或最佳标准）
words.ex: The gold standard was abandoned in the 20th century.
words.ex_cn: 金本位在20世纪被废除。
words.en: A gold standard is a monetary system where a country's currency or paper money has a value directly linked to gold. It can also refer to the best example of something against which others are judged.

words.tr: phrase. 政府智囊团；指为政府提供政策建议和研究支持的专门机构
words.ex: The government think-tank gave advice on new laws.
words.ex_cn: 政府智库就新法律提供了建议。
words.en: A government think-tank is a group of experts who are employed by the government to provide advice and ideas on political, social, and economic issues.

words.tr: phrase. 对冲基金；一种采用多种投资策略以规避风险并获取高回报的私募投资基金
words.ex: He works for a hedge fund in New York.
words.ex_cn: 他在纽约的一家对冲基金工作。
words.en: Hedge funds are investment funds that trade relatively liquid assets and can use a wide variety of trading strategies to improve performance, such as short selling, leverage, and derivatives.

words.tr: phrase. 房地产市场；住房市场
words.ex: The housing market is getting more expensive.
words.ex_cn: 房地产市场正在变得越来越贵。
words.en: The housing market refers to the supply and demand for houses, usually in a particular country or region. It includes the buying, selling, and renting of homes.

words.tr: phrase. 在步履蹒跚的经济中；处于衰退的经济环境下
words.ex: Many families struggle in a faltering economy.
words.ex_cn: 在经济疲软时，许多家庭感到艰难。
words.en: In an economy that is struggling or declining.

words.tr: phrase. 工业产出下降；工业产量减少
words.ex: Industrial output falls this month due to low demand.
words.ex_cn: 由于需求低迷，本月工业产出下降。
words.en: The amount of goods produced by factories decreases.

words.ex: The company will lay off employees because of low sales.
words.ex_cn: 由于销售额低，公司将会裁员。
words.en: To dismiss workers from their jobs, often due to financial difficulties.

words.ex: Our country has a mixed economy with both private and government businesses.
words.ex_cn: 我们的国家拥有混合经济，既有私营企业也有政府企业。
words.en: A mixed economy is an economic system that combines private and public enterprise, allowing for both market forces and government intervention.

words.ex: The bank changed its monetary policy to control inflation.
words.ex_cn: 银行改变了货币政策以控制通货膨胀。
words.en: Monetary policy refers to the actions of a central bank, currency board or other regulatory committee that determine the size and rate of growth of the money supply, which in turn affects interest rates. Monetary policy is maintained through actions such as modifying the interest rate, buying or selling government bonds, and changing the amount of money banks are required to keep in the vault (bank reserves).

words.tr: phrase. 洗钱（把非法所得伪装成合法收入的行为）
words.ex: He was arrested for money laundering.
words.ex_cn: 他因洗钱被逮捕了。
words.en: Money laundering is the process of concealing the origin of money obtained from illicit activities such as drug trafficking, corruption, or embezzlement, by channeling it through a sequence of banking transfers or commercial transactions.

words.ex: The bank controls the money supply.
words.ex_cn: 银行控制货币供应。
words.en: The total amount of money available in an economy at a particular time.

words.tr: phrase. 道德风险；因缺乏有效约束而导致一方在获得保障后采取更高风险行为的经济现象
words.ex: The bank took big risks because it thought the government would save it — that's moral hazard.
words.ex_cn: 银行承担了巨大风险，因为它认为政府会拯救它——这就是道德风险。
words.en: A situation where a party is more likely to take risks because the negative consequences of those risks will be borne, at least in part, by another party.

words.ex: The government started nationalization of the oil companies.
words.ex_cn: 政府开始对石油公司进行国有化。
words.en: The process by which a government takes control of a private industry or assets and brings them under state ownership.

words.tr: phrase. 净资产；净值（资产总额减去负债总额后的剩余价值）
words.ex: His net worth is one million dollars.
words.ex_cn: 他的净资产是一百万美元。
words.en: The total value of all assets owned by an individual or corporation, minus any liabilities.

words.ex: The country uses non-tariff barrier to limit imports.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家使用非关税壁垒来限制进口。
words.en: A non-tariff barrier is a way to restrict trade using trade barriers in a form other than a tariff. Non-tariff barriers include quotas, embargoes, sanctions, and levies.

words.tr: n. [热]过热; v. [热]过热（overheat 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The engine suffered from overheating after running too long.
words.ex_cn: 发动机因长时间运行而过热。
words.en: If something overheats or if you overheat it, it becomes hotter than is necessary or desirable.

words.tr: n. 决策者；政策制定者
words.ex: The policymaker made a new rule for schools.
words.ex_cn: 这位政策制定者为学校制定了一项新规定。
words.en: A policymaker is a person responsible for or involved in formulating policies, especially in government.

words.tr: phrase. 物价指数；价格指数；用于衡量一组商品或服务价格水平随时间变化的指标
words.ex: The price index shows a significant increase this year.
words.ex_cn: 物价指数显示今年有显著增长。
words.en: A price index is a normalized average of price relatives for a given class of goods or services in a given region, during a given period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 支撑；撑住；扶持；维持（不稳定的局面或体系）
words.ex: They use a stick to prop up the broken tree.
words.ex_cn: 他们用一根棍子撑起那棵断了的树。
words.en: To prop up something means to support it or keep it in position by placing something underneath or against it.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.tr: phrase. 互惠贸易协定；两国或多国间相互降低关税及贸易壁垒的正式协议
words.ex: The two countries entered into a reciprocal trade agreement to boost economic cooperation.
words.ex_cn: 两国签订了互惠贸易协定以促进经济合作。
words.en: A reciprocal trade agreement is a pact between two or more countries to mutually reduce or eliminate trade barriers, such as tariffs and quotas, to increase trade and economic cooperation.

words.tr: phrase. 救援计划；营救方案；拯救计划
words.ex: The government made a rescue plan for the failing company.
words.ex_cn: 政府为这家陷入困境的公司制定了救援计划。
words.en: A rescue plan is a set of actions designed to save or help someone or something from a difficult or dangerous situation.

words.tr: phrase. 设定一个目标；确立一个目的
words.ex: He set a goal to run every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他设定了每天早上跑步的目标。
words.en: To decide on something you want to achieve and plan how to achieve it.

words.ex: There is a shortfall in food supplies this winter.
words.ex_cn: 今年冬天食物供应不足。
words.en: A shortfall is a situation in which there is not enough of something, especially money.

words.tr: phrase. 主权财富基金：由国家政府建立并管理的用于投资的基金，通常来源于国家财政盈余、外汇储备或自然资源收入
words.ex: The country uses its sovereign wealth fund to buy foreign stocks.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家用它的主权财富基金购买外国股票。
words.en: A sovereign wealth fund is a state-owned investment fund or entity that is commonly established from balance of payments surpluses, official foreign currency operations, the proceeds of privatizations, governmental transfer payments, fiscal surpluses, and/or receipts resulting from resource exports.

words.tr:
n. 库存；股票；家畜；
v. 备有；贮存；
words.ex: The store has low stock of winter coats.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的冬衣库存很少。
words.en: The supply of goods available for sale in a store; the capital raised by a company through the issue of shares.

words.tr: phrase. 贸易保护主义：指国家通过关税、配额等手段限制进口，以保护本国产业免受外国竞争影响的经济政策
words.ex: The government uses trade protectionism to help local factories.
words.ex_cn: 政府使用贸易保护主义来帮助本地工厂。
words.en: Trade protectionism refers to economic policies that restrict imports from other countries through methods such as tariffs on imported goods, import quotas, and a variety of other government regulations. These policies are intended to protect domestic industries and jobs from foreign competition.

words.tr: phrase. 工资削减；薪资缩减
words.ex: The company announced wage cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司宣布削减工资以节省开支。
words.en: A reduction in the amount of money that employees are paid.

words.tr: phrase. 批发商；批发经销商
words.ex: The wholesale dealer supplies goods to retail stores.
words.ex_cn: 批发商向零售店供应商品。
words.en: A wholesale dealer is a person or company that sells goods in large quantities at low prices, typically to be sold on by retailers at a profit.

chapters.name: 主题分类词汇 环境、灾害类

words.ex: He had an accidental fall while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他在走路时不小心摔了一跤。
words.en: An accidental event happens by chance, without being planned.

words.ex: The aftershock shook the house again.
words.ex_cn: 余震再次震动了房子。
words.en: An aftershock is a smaller earthquake that occurs after a previous large earthquake, in the same area of the main shock.

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

words.ex: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: A catastrophic event or situation is one that causes great damage or suffering.

words.ex: The charity helps poor children get food and education.
words.ex_cn: 这个慈善团体帮助贫困儿童获得食物和教育。
words.en: An organization that helps people in need, or the act of giving money, food, or help to those who need it.

words.tr:
v. 声称；索赔；
n. 声称；索要；
words.ex: He claims that he saw a UFO last night.
words.ex_cn: 他声称自己昨晚看到了不明飞行物。
words.en: If you say that someone claims that something is true, you mean they say that it is true but you are not sure whether or not they are telling the truth.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.ex: The car crash was a serious collision.
words.ex_cn: 那场车祸是一次严重的碰撞。
words.en: A collision occurs when two or more objects come into contact with each other, often resulting in damage or a change in direction.

words.tr: n. 毁灭；引起毁灭的根源；
words.ex: The storm caused the destruction of the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: The act of destroying something, or the state of being destroyed.

words.ex: The earthquake caused a big disaster.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了一场大灾难。
words.en: A disaster is an unexpected event causing great damage, destruction, or distress.

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: The drought made it hard to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 旱灾使种植庄稼变得困难。
words.en: A drought is a long period of time during which no rain falls and hence there is a shortage of water.

words.ex: A bird emerged from the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一只鸟从树中浮现出来。
words.en: If something or someone emerges, they come out of or move out of something and become visible.

words.ex: The village suffered from famine last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个村庄遭受了饥荒。
words.en: A famine is a serious shortage of food in a country, which may cause many people to get sick or die.

words.ex: The accident was fatal.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是致命的。
words.en: If an action or event is fatal, it causes someone's death.

words.tr:
n. 火焰
v. 燃烧；爆发；面红
words.ex: The candle flame flickered in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 蜡烛的火焰在风中摇曳。
words.en: A flame is a hot bright stream of burning gas that comes from something that is burning.

words.ex: The foundation gives money to poor students.
words.ex_cn: 这个基金会向贫困学生提供资金。
words.en: The foundation of something such as a belief or way of life is the things on which it is based.

words.ex: The broken glass is a hazard.
words.ex_cn: 碎玻璃是危险。
words.en: A hazard is something which could be dangerous to you, your health or safety, or your plans or reputation.

words.ex: The virus can infect people quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒能迅速感染人。
words.en: To infect someone or something means to cause them to have a disease or illness.

words.ex: He injured his leg while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时伤了腿。
words.en: To injure someone means to cause them physical harm, for example in an accident or an attack.

words.ex: The farm stopped selling beef because of mad cow disease.
words.ex_cn: 由于疯牛病，这个农场停止销售牛肉。
words.en: Mad cow disease, also known as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), is a neurodegenerative disease in cattle that causes a spongy degeneration in the brain and spinal cord.

words.ex: He felt miserable after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后感到很悲惨。
words.en: If you are miserable, you are very unhappy.

words.ex: The refugee walked to a new country.
words.ex_cn: 这名难民步行去了一个新国家。
words.en: A refugee is a person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster.

words.tr:
n. 救援；营救；
v. 救援；营救；
words.ex: The rescue came just in time to save the hikers.
words.ex_cn: 救援及时赶到，救出了徒步者。
words.en: To rescue someone or something means to save them from a dangerous or unpleasant situation.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.tr:
v. 传播；扩散；散布；
n. 传播；蔓延；范围；
words.ex: The virus spread quickly through the city.
words.ex_cn: 病毒在城市中迅速传播。
words.en: To spread something means to open it out or arrange it over a place or surface, so that all of it can be seen or used easily.

words.tr: v. 幸存；生存；存活；艰难挺过；
words.ex: He survived the accident with minor injuries.
words.ex_cn: 他在事故中幸存下来，只有轻微受伤。
words.en: If you survive in a dangerous situation, you continue to live or exist in spite of it.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.ex: He did voluntary work at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院做志愿工作。
words.en: If something is voluntary, you do it because you choose to, and not because you have to.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

words.ex: The government provides welfare to poor families.
words.ex_cn: 政府向贫困家庭提供福利。
words.en: The welfare of a person or group is their health, comfort, and happiness.

words.tr:
n. 遇难船只；残骸；
v. 破坏；毁坏；
words.ex: The wreck lies at the bottom of the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这艘遇难船只沉在海底。
words.en: If something such as a ship or a plane is wrecked, it is damaged so much that it cannot be repaired or it is completely destroyed.

words.ex: He finally acknowledged his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you acknowledge a fact or a situation, you accept or admit that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.ex: He affirm that the plan will work.
words.ex_cn: 他断言这个计划会成功。
